_meta.purpose: Current-state discovery for Business Architecture: an L3 questionnaire template, generated contextual questions, and demo survey responses. L2 Process / Technology / Data / Integration / Business criticality are inferred from L3 answers when the L2 is analysed.
_meta.note: Demo responses are illustrative and calibrated so the inferred L2 scores equal the assumed seed baseline. Replace with real owner responses. Owner names are roles; emails are left blank until confirmed.
_meta.inference: Dimension score = mean of L3 answers rounded half up; business criticality = highest L3 answer; business-IT alignment = mean of the five alignment questions (system fit, partnering, information & reporting, responsiveness to change, user adoption).

template.label: Business owner
template.text: Who is accountable for {l3}, and which team performs it day to day?
template.help: Name the role accountable for outcomes (not the system owner), plus the team and approximate headcount that execute it.

template.label: Systems & tools
template.text: Which systems, tools or files are used to perform {l3}?
template.help: Tick every application involved and list anything else: Excel trackers, email, WhatsApp groups, government portals.

template.label: Process standardisation
template.text: How is {l3} documented and measured across plants, regions and entities?
template.help: Think about whether two regions would run it the same way, and whether anyone reviews a KPI for it each month.
options: Not documented; depends on individuals
Local SOPs or desk notes that vary by site
One enterprise SOP, followed consistently
Enterprise SOP with KPIs reviewed monthly by an owner
KPIs benchmarked and continuously improved

template.label: Technology & AI enablement
template.text: How is the work in {l3} executed in those systems?
template.help: Pick the level that describes most of the volume, not the best-case pilot.
options: Paper, Excel, email or WhatsApp
Recorded in a system of record; checks and hand-offs manual
Workflow, rules or RPA automate most steps
AI / ML recommends; people decide
AI agents execute steps within guardrails; people supervise exceptions

template.label: Data availability & trust
template.text: How available and trusted is the data {l3} depends on?
template.help: Consider how often numbers are reconciled by hand before they are used, and whether a single owner signs them off.
options: Missing or unreliable; re-collected each time
Available but scattered; reconciled manually
Owned, with defined quality rules
Single trusted source reused across functions
Near real-time with lineage; ready for analytics and AI

template.label: Integration & hand-offs
template.text: How does {l3} hand off to upstream and downstream processes and systems?
template.help: Follow one transaction: is anything typed twice, uploaded as a file, or passed through an interface?
options: Re-keyed manually between systems
File uploads or scheduled batch
Direct point-to-point interfaces
Governed APIs or events
Orchestrated end to end with monitoring

template.label: System fit (business–IT alignment)
template.text: How well do the current systems fit what {l3} needs?
template.help: Count the workarounds: offline trackers, manual checks, or steps done outside the system because it cannot support them.
options: Major workarounds outside the system
Partial fit; frequent manual workarounds
Adequate fit; known gaps tolerated
Good fit; minor enhancements pending
Full fit; the system drives the process

template.label: Business–IT partnering (business–IT alignment)
template.text: How do business and IT work together on changes to {l3}?
template.help: Is there a named IT counterpart, a shared backlog, and an agreed, funded roadmap?
options: No IT counterpart; changes are ad hoc
IT engaged reactively through tickets
Named IT counterpart and a joint backlog
Joint roadmap with agreed priorities and funding
Product team (business + IT) with shared outcomes

template.label: Information & reporting support (business–IT alignment)
template.text: How well do the systems give you the information you need to run and steer {l3}?
template.help: Think about the last monthly review: did the numbers come straight from a system, or were they assembled by hand?
options: No system reporting; numbers are compiled by hand
Basic extracts; most analysis is rebuilt in Excel
Standard reports cover the main KPIs
Self-service dashboards with trusted, timely data
Real-time insight with alerts and recommendations

template.label: IT responsiveness to change (business–IT alignment)
template.text: When {l3} needs a change in a system, how quickly and predictably does IT deliver it?
template.help: Take a recent request, such as a new field, report or rule change, and how long it took from request to go-live.
options: Changes rarely happen or take more than six months
Months, with unclear priority
Weeks, through an agreed release cycle
Days to weeks, prioritised jointly with the business
Continuous delivery; the business can configure most changes itself

template.label: User adoption (business–IT alignment)
template.text: How consistently do the people performing {l3} work in the system rather than around it?
template.help: Consider plants, regions and field teams: is the system the single place the work is recorded?
options: Systems are largely bypassed
Used for the final record only; the work happens outside
Used by most teams with some local workarounds
Used consistently across sites and teams
Embedded in daily work; users push for more capability

template.label: Peak-season performance (scalability)
template.text: How do the systems behind {l3} cope at peak season (kharif and rabi) or month-end?
template.help: Think of the busiest week last season: did screens slow down, batches overrun or teams switch to offline workarounds?
options: Fails; we switch to manual workarounds
Slows badly; deadlines slip
Slows but copes
Copes with minor delays
No impact at peak

template.label: Fallback if a system or person is unavailable (single points of failure)
template.text: If the main system or the one person who knows it is unavailable, can {l3} continue?
template.help: Consider an outage of a day, or the key user or vendor resource being away for a week.
options: Stops completely; no fallback
Continues only on paper or Excel
A manual fallback exists but is untested
Tested fallback for most scenarios
Fully redundant; no single person or system

template.label: Workarounds and fixes (technical debt)
template.text: How much effort goes into workarounds, patches or reconciliations to keep {l3} running?
template.help: Count recurring fixes, custom scripts, manual reconciliations and change requests waiting on old code.
options: Constant firefighting; changes are risky
Frequent fixes and reconciliations
Some known workarounds
Rare; changes are routine
None; the platform is clean and current

template.label: Business criticality
template.text: How critical is {l3} to Coromandel's business and its 2030 strategy?
template.help: High means it directly moves revenue, margin, farmer reach or regulatory compliance (subsidy, DPDP, CIB&RC).
options: Peripheral
Supporting
Important
High: directly affects revenue, margin or compliance
Critical: differentiating or a regulatory must-have
